More context:

Kansas City has an earnings tax, if you live or work in Kansas City you pay 1% of your income in taxes. The idea being that people who use the infrastructure should pay for the upkeep. It makes up about 45% of the general fund and 15% of the overall city budget. About 40% of the tax comes from non-residents.

But a few years ago Missouri had a ballot initiative which outlawed new earnings taxes from being implemented and required that existing ones be put up for renewal every so often. (If the tax is not renewed then it's phased out over a 10 year period.) The catch is that only Kansas City residents can vote on the renewal of the earnings tax, which means the people who provide 40% of the tax can't vote on it.

So those people have been doing their damnedest (including one millionaire in particular who pushed for the original ballot initiative) to make sure that residents let them off the hook for that tax.

The thing they leave out, of course, is the fact that the city will just replace the massive gap in the budget (even if it is just phased out over 10 years) with a massive increase in either sales or property taxes, the former is regressive and the latter hits retirees who didn't qualify for the earnings tax and lets all the non-residents who help pay for the infrastructure they used off the hook.

So basically people who can't vote on something are trying to convince people who can vote on it to increase their own taxes while eliminating the taxes on the people who can't vote on something.
In Kansas City, millionaires who pay a tax, but can't vote on it are trying to convince people who pay the tax, but can vote on it to repeal it so the city can increase taxes on only those people.
